response:
READING

**Budget and timeline arithmetic**

The bequest is GBP 340,000, hard-stopped at 2028-09-30. The Threlkeld quote of GBP 295,000 is held only to 2027-01-30. Commissioning is 2027-05-29, and Threlkeld need the order fourteen weeks ahead of that, which works back to approximately 20 February 2027. Placing the order by 30 January 2027 (quote expiry) gives roughly 17–18 weeks of lead time, which exceeds the required 14 weeks and still locks in the quoted price. Today is 2026-08-25, so about five months remain to reach that decision. The window is not comfortable, but it is real.

Under HAVERSHOLT the spend is GBP 295,000 + GBP 45,000 = GBP 340,000, the full bequest. GBP 45,000 ÷ GBP 250 per item = 180 items of conservation. If ordered alongside the plant in late January 2027, conservation starts around late March 2027 and 180 items at 70 per month run off in roughly 2.5 months, completing around June 2027 — well inside the 2028 deadline.

Under LINDCASTER the spend is GBP 340,000 ÷ GBP 250 = 1,360 items. At 70 items per month, starting eight weeks after an order placed now (approximately late October 2026), the programme runs roughly 19.4 months, finishing around mid-2028 — also inside the deadline.

Both courses are arithmetically clean and deliverable within the grant window.

---

**The conservator's written report**

This is the most important single piece of evidence in the file. Idris Sankey-Marchmont states in writing that rehousing and aqueous treatment carried out into the strongroom as it stands will need to be repeated within a decade. That statement is not a caution; it is a professional opinion in writing that LINDCASTER's GBP 340,000 is a consumable. The institute would be purchasing temporary relief, not a solution. A decade from the start of treatment is approximately 2036–2037. The environment is not expected to improve under LINDCASTER until 2029–30 at the earliest, and possibly not at all if the capital programme allocates elsewhere. The gap between treatment and plant installation — three to four years — means items are held in enclosures at high humidity for that whole period; the eight-to-twelve year enclosure clock then starts from an already compromised baseline.

---

**What the buffered enclosures actually do**

The stated property is that they hold an item's microclimate within 3 points of its packing condition. The packing condition is the strongroom: approximately 62 per cent RH. Holding within 3 points means the items experience roughly 59–65 per cent RH. That is still 7–10 points above the top of the target range (55 per cent) and far outside the 45–55 standard. The enclosures damp the 11-point seasonal swing, which is valuable, but they do not solve the level problem. They slow, they do not stop. The conservator's opinion about repetition is consistent with this: the treatment buys time, not permanence.

---

**What the 2029–30 capital programme is**

Under LINDCASTER, GBP 400,000 of unallocated, uncommitted capital — set by a board in November 2028, two years from now — is the load-bearing element for fixing the root cause. That money could go anywhere. An infrastructure failure, a roof, a competing collection need: none of these is unlikely over two years at an institution of this type. If that board meeting does not allocate the money, the strongroom never gets plant, the 1,360 items treated under LINDCASTER enter their second cycle needing retreatment, and the institute has spent GBP 340,000 for a temporary improvement in conditions for less than a third of the collection.

Under HAVERSHOLT, the same unallocated line would fund conservation in a stable environment. If it fails to materialise, 4,200 items are nonetheless held at 45–55 per cent RH in a controlled swing from mid-2027 onward. The clock has stopped. The loss is forgone conservation volume, not continued physical deterioration.

HAVERSHOLT is more resilient to the 2029–30 line failing than LINDCASTER is.

---

**The deterioration rate and coverage**

The 2025 resurvey puts 1,010 items in the unusable band, against 640 in 2019: 370 items in six years, about 62 per year. LINDCASTER's implicit argument is that these items are being lost now and only treatment can reach them. That is true. But under HAVERSHOLT, the plant commissions May 2027 — roughly nine months from now — and the environmental clock stops for all 4,200 items at that point. Under LINDCASTER, the environment does not stabilise until 2029–30 at earliest, adding perhaps another 186–248 items to the unusable band before the root cause is addressed.

LINDCASTER does treat 1,360 items immediately against HAVERSHOLT's 180 items, and that gap is real. But if the conservator is right that treatment in the current environment needs repeating, those 1,360 are treated twice at GBP 250 each, costing an effective GBP 500 per item for a permanently stable result — and only then because the plant has arrived. Under HAVERSHOLT, treatment from the 2029–30 programme (if it comes) costs GBP 250 per item and does not need repeating.

---

**Quote risk**

If LINDCASTER is chosen, the Threlkeld quote for GBP 295,000 lapses on 2027-01-30 and the market is re-entered in 2028–29 for a new procurement. Construction and M&E plant costs have moved materially in recent years. There is no guarantee that equivalent plant is available within GBP 400,000 by 2029–30. Under HAVERSHOLT the price is locked, confirmed in writing, and the order deadline is achievable.

---

**Summary of the comparison**

| Factor | HAVERSHOLT | LINDCASTER |
|---|---|---|
| Items treated permanently within bequest | 180 (in good environment) | ~0 (conservator says needs repeating) |
| Items whose environment is stabilised | 4,200 from May 2027 | 1,360 partially (at 59–65% RH) |
| Reliance on 2029–30 unallocated line | For conservation (more natural capital use; failure leaves 4,200 in stable conditions) | For plant (failure leaves environment unfixed indefinitely) |
| Conservator's written assessment | Favourable (nothing commissioned twice) | Unfavourable (treatment needs repeating) |
| Quote risk | None, if ordered by 2027-01-30 | Re-procurement in 2029 at unknown price |
| Years of additional loss before root cause fixed | ~9 months (~47 items) | ~3–4 years (~186–248 items) |

HAVERSHOLT involves accepting that only 180 items receive conservation under the current bequest. That is a genuine cost. But the conservator has told the institute in writing that money spent on conservation in the existing environment is time-limited. Spending GBP 340,000 on work that must be repeated is not conservation strategy; it is deferred expenditure at full price. The locked quote at GBP 295,000 and the certainty of the commissioning date give the institute a defined, costed path to a permanent environmental standard for the whole collection, after which all future conservation spend — whether from the 2029–30 programme or another source — produces results that do not expire.

---

CALL
  HAVERSHOLT

GROUNDS
  The conservator's written statement that treatment in the existing environment will need repeating within a decade renders LINDCASTER's GBP 340,000 a time-limited expenditure rather than a solution, while HAVERSHOLT fixes the root cause before the Threlkeld quote lapses and ensures that every pound of future conservation spend — including any drawn from the 2029–30 capital line — produces a permanent result in a stable environment.
